title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
title_zh: SimXAI：一个简单的即插即用层，提升会话式可解释AI的交互质量与理解能力

paragraphs.en: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. These pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. We present SimXAI , a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces these modules with a single tool-calling LLM that bridges access to existing XAI resources. Rather than a standalone agent, SimXAI serves as a modular interface that enables conversational access to external XAI resources. We further introduce an evaluation suite for single- and multi-turn parsing, response-to-tool faithfulness, and contextualization. Across existing and new datasets, SimXAI achieves strong function-selection accuracy and high response-to-tool faithfulness while better handling context-dependent requests. In a user study replacing only the conversational layer of TalkToModel , a representative GUS-based agent, users completed tasks more accurately and in fewer turns. Overall, SimXAI improves conversational interaction while leaving the underlying XAI resources unchanged 1 1 1 The source code (including evaluation suite) is available at: https://github.com/bach-mr/SimXAI .

paragraphs.en: The XAI community has reached a consensus that explanations should take a conversational form Miller (2019) ; Lakkaraju et al. (2022) ; Zhang et al. (2025) . Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents therefore move beyond one-off explanations and embrace conversational approaches to provide explanations. These conversational explanations have been demonstrated to be more effective for users’ model understanding Shen et al. (2023) ; Mindlin et al. (2024) ; He et al. (2025) . Conceptually, a ConvXAI agent can be decomposed into two parts: (i) a conversational layer ( ConvXAI layer ), responsible for managing the interaction with the user, and (ii) the underlying XAI resources , which store or generate the explanatory information (e.g., model/data cards Mitchell et al. (2019) ; Pushkarna et al. (2022) , or feature-attribution methods like SHAP Lundberg and Lee (2017) or counterfactual explanations Mothilal et al. (2020) ; Ross et al. (2021) ). Most current ConvXAI agents (i.a., Nguyen et al. 2023 ; Slack et al. 2023 ; Feldhus et al. 2023 ; Wang et al. 2024a ) adopt the traditional GUS (Genial Understanding System) architecture Bobrow et al. (1977) for the ConvXAI layer, which comprises three distinct components: natural language understanding (NLU) for intent recognition, dialogue management for context maintenance and rule application, and natural language generation (NLG) for response production. Although such GUS-based ConvXAI layers present explanations through interactive dialogue, they rely on multiple models separately fine-tuned on handcrafted data for intent recognition in NLU, rule-based dialogue management, and template-based response generation in NLG (Figure 1 ). As a result, they remain limited in contextualization, scalability, and generalization Rastogi et al. (2020) . These limitations highlight the need for lightweight, adaptive, and flexible ConvXAI layers. Recent developments suggest that LLMs can fulfill this role and replace traditional ConvXAI layers in such systems Li et al. (2024) .

paragraphs.en: We introduce SimXAI , a simple, lightweight, LLM-centric framework that acts as a ConvXAI layer between users and existing XAI resources (see Figure 1 ). Unlike rule- or template-based systems, SimXAI uses an LLM to support natural, context-aware dialogue without requiring handcrafted intent datasets or conversational fine-tuning. The layer is data- and model-agnostic . Integrating it into an agent requires only function implementations that provide access to the agent’s existing XAI resources. SimXAI can therefore replace the conversational components of GUS-based agents (e.g., Slack et al. 2023 ; Nguyen et al. 2023 ) while preserving the underlying explanations. SimXAI is not a standalone agent and does not itself select or validate XAI methods. Instead, it provides a modular interface to resources supplied by the host system.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 SimXAI，这是一个简单、轻量、以大语言模型（LLM）为中心的框架，它在用户与现有 XAI 资源之间充当一个 ConvXAI 层（见图 1）。 与基于规则或模板的系统不同，SimXAI 使用大语言模型来支持自然且具备上下文感知能力的对话，而无需人工构建意图数据集或进行对话微调。 该层与数据和模型无关。 将其集成到一个智能体中，只需要实现若干函数，用于访问该智能体已有的 XAI 资源。 因此，SimXAI 可以取代基于 GUS 的智能体（例如 Slack et al. 2023；Nguyen et al. 2023）中的对话组件，同时保留底层的解释。 SimXAI 不是一个独立的智能体，它本身不选择或验证 XAI 方法。 相反，它为宿主系统提供的资源提供一个模块化接口。

paragraphs.en: Prior work on evaluating ConvXAI has mainly focused on isolated turns Malandri et al. (2023) ; Wang et al. (2024a) and has often overlooked dialogue context. To address this gap, we evaluate SimXAI on parsing accuracy in single- and multi-turn dialogues, contextualization, and response-to-tool faithfulness. For each aspect, we provide a dataset with manually annotated ground truth, corresponding metrics, and an automated evaluation pipeline. The faithfulness evaluation measures whether the conversational layer preserves the returned XAI output. It does not measure whether the underlying explanation method is faithful to the predictive model.

paragraphs.en: In summary, our contributions are threefold. First , based on the analysis of limitations of prior work (§ 2 ), we introduce SimXAI , an LLM-centric framework that addresses these limitations and offers a practical alternative to conventional ConvXAI layers (§ 3 ). Second , we present a multi-aspect evaluation suite for ConvXAI layers, including automated assessment of parsing, response-to-tool faithfulness, and contextualization (§ 4 ). Third , we show through quantitative evaluation and a user study that replacing a conventional conversational layer with SimXAI improves significantly conversational quality while preserving faithfulness to underlying XAI outputs (§ 5 , § 6 ).

paragraphs.en: GUS-based ConvXAI layers (such as Nguyen et al. 2023 ; Slack et al. 2023 ; Feldhus et al. 2023 ) support follow-up questions, but their conversational behavior is typically implemented through task-specific grammars, intent schemas, templates, or dialogue rules. As summarized in Table 1 , this design leads to a recurring trade-off between faithfulness and three other dimensions: contextualization , scalability , and generalization .

paragraphs.en: At the same time, these constrained designs maximally preserve faithfulness in response generation. As they generate outputs through rules or templates, the conversational layer is less likely to introduce unsupported claims or misrepresent the underlying XAI method results. paragraphs.en: SimXAI adds a conversational interface to existing XAI resources using only two components: (1) an off-the-shelf LLM with tool-calling support and (2) a set of general function specifications that map user requests onto available XAI resources. The novelty lies in this ConvXAI-specific separation and interface, rather than in the general mechanism of LLM tool calling. Unlike prior systems, SimXAI does not rely on task-specific grammars, intent schemas, dialogue managers, or response templates. Instead, SimXAI interprets the current user query together with the dialogue history, selects the appropriate function, fills its arguments from context when applicable, and verbalizes the returned result. The backend remains responsible for computing the prediction, explanation, or data/model information returned by that function.
paragraphs.zh: SimXAI 仅通过两个组件为现有的 XAI 资源添加对话式接口：(1) 一个支持工具调用的现成大语言模型，以及 (2) 一组通用函数规范，将用户请求映射到可用的 XAI 资源上。 其新颖之处在于这种 ConvXAI 特定的分离与接口，而不是大语言模型工具调用这一通用机制。 与先前的系统不同，SimXAI 不依赖于特定任务的语法、意图模式、对话管理器或响应模板。 相反，SimXAI 结合对话历史来解释当前的用户查询，选择合适的函数，在适用时从上下文中填充其参数，并将返回的结果转化为自然语言表述。 后端仍然负责计算该函数所返回的预测、解释或数据/模型信息。

paragraphs.en: Our set of functions is based on the question bank of Liao and Varshney (2022) ; Liao et al. (2020) . This question bank was created from practitioner interviews and organized around model-, data-, and context-related questions about AI systems. From this bank, we implement 11 functions: one retrieves the model prediction for a given instance and the other ten address explanatory questions, such as why the model made a particular prediction or how to modify an instance to change the prediction. For each function, we specify its purpose, inputs, arguments, and outputs. Table 2 summarizes the full set. The set is extensible: if no predefined function matches a user’s intent, a new function can be added with its own specification ( Figure 2 ).

For each function, we adopt a standard specification template ( Figure 2 ) that defines the function name, argument list and types, documentation, and expected input and output types. Figure 5 in the appendix for a concrete example of a counterfactual function specification).

paragraphs.en: We evaluate ConvXAI layers along three aspects: parsing , response-to-tool faithfulness , and contextualization . Parsing measures whether the system selects the correct function and arguments for a user request, response-to-tool faithfulness measures whether the final response is supported by the returned XAI output, and contextualization measures whether the system uses dialogue history appropriately when interpreting the current turn. Table 4 summarizes the evaluation suite. This scope evaluates the conversational layer only: it neither measures nor guarantees the intrinsic correctness or model-faithfulness of the backend XAI method that produced the tool output. We use this suite for two purposes. First, we assess SimXAI directly across settings of increasing conversational complexity. Second, we qualitatively analyze gains from replacing the conversational components of prior GUS-based ConvXAI systems with SimXAI while keeping their underlying XAI resources unchanged.

paragraphs.en: To evaluate long-range dependencies, we generate synthetic dialogue-level datasets in two domains: sentiment analysis SYN-Sentiment and heart rate prediction SYN-HeartRate . Each of the two datasets combines dialogues generated under two settings: Constrained , in which we provide our 11 function specifications in the prompt and ask GPT-5.1 to generate realistic conversations covering all operations, and Unconstrained , in which GPT-5.1 is prompted to generate realistic conversations without any predefined constraints. Each user turn defines one parsing instance, with the full preceding dialogue provided as context. Human validation assessed these synthetic dialogues as mostly realistic (details in Appendix B ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估长距离依赖，我们在两个领域中生成了合成的对话级数据集：情感分析 SYN-Sentiment 和心率预测 SYN-HeartRate。 这两个数据集各自结合了在两种设置下生成的对话：受限设置（Constrained），即我们在提示中提供 11 个函数规范，并要求 GPT-5.1 生成覆盖所有操作的真实对话；以及非受限设置（Unconstrained），即在不施加任何预定义约束的情况下提示 GPT-5.1 生成真实对话。 每个用户回合定义一个解析实例，并将之前的完整对话作为上下文提供。 人工验证认为这些合成对话大多符合真实情况（详见附录 B）。

paragraphs.en: As LLMs are prone to hallucination Huang et al. (2025) , we evaluate the faithfulness of the agent’s responses with respect to the provided XAI resources. (2024) , we define response-to-tool faithfulness as the extent to which the conversational layer preserves the information contained in a returned XAI output without introducing unsupported claims. This is distinct from the intrinsic faithfulness of the XAI method to the predictive model, which is outside our scope.

paragraphs.en: Contextualization evaluates whether the system uses dialogue history appropriately to answer the current query. We first assess context relevance by manually determining whether a query can be answered independently or requires the preceding dialogue. For queries that depend on prior context, we then assess whether the response incorporates the necessary dialogue history to resolve the current turn coherently. This contextual answer coherence is a binary judgment, aggregated as accuracy (the fraction of contextually coherent answers).
paragraphs.zh: 语境化评估系统是否恰当地利用对话历史来回答当前查询。 我们首先通过人工判断某个查询能否独立回答、还是需要依赖前文对话，来评估上下文相关性。 对于依赖先前上下文的查询，我们随后评估回复是否融入了必要的对话历史，以连贯地解决当前轮次。 这一语境化答案连贯性是一项二元判断，以准确率（语境连贯答案所占比例）进行汇总。

paragraphs.en: In most cases (over 91%), SimXAI produces responses that are faithful to the tool output , indicating that the conversational layer preserves the returned XAI information rather than introducing unsupported claims. This is particularly important because SimXAI replaces rule- and template-based conversational components with an LLM-based interface, which may increase the risk of hallucinations. These results do not evaluate the intrinsic faithfulness of the backend XAI methods.
paragraphs.zh: 在大多数情况下（超过91%），SimXAI 生成的回复与工具输出保持一致，这表明对话层保留了返回的 XAI 信息，而没有引入缺乏依据的断言。 这一点尤为重要，因为 SimXAI 用基于大语言模型的接口取代了基于规则和模板的对话组件，而这可能会增加幻觉的风险。 这些结果并未评估后端 XAI 方法本身的忠实性。

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 shows an example failure case of incorrect context handling of TalkToModel ’s native conversational layers. TalkToModel fails to maintain contextual understanding because the agent misinterprets the referent of “it” (anaphora), which leads to an incorrect final decision. Replacing TalkToModel ’s conversational layers by SimXAI fixes this issue and correctly resolves the context in the same conversation dialogue. We observe similar patterns of incorrect context handling in the other agents under comparison, which are partially unable to provide an answer at all. Replacing the conversational layers of these agents by SimXAI corrects such issues (examples in Appendix C ).
paragraphs.zh: 图 1 展示了 TalkToModel 原生对话层在上下文处理上的一个错误失败案例。 TalkToModel 未能保持对上下文的理解，因为智能体误解了“it”的指代对象（回指），从而导致最终的错误决策。 用 SimXAI 替换 TalkToModel 的对话层可以解决这一问题，并在同一对话中正确解析上下文。 我们在其他被比较的智能体中也观察到类似的上下文处理错误模式，它们部分甚至完全无法给出答案。 用 SimXAI 替换这些智能体的对话层可以纠正此类问题（示例见附录 C）。

paragraphs.en: For each agent, participants complete three tasks. These tasks cover multiple categories from an established XAI question taxonomy Liao et al. (2020) , including data understanding, local explanations, and counterfactual inspection. Each task contains at least two questions, for a total of nine questions across all tasks. The questions are sampled from a pool of predefined multiple-choice questions for each task (details in Appendix Section D.1 ). They are designed to be answerable using the ground-truth information provided by the agent’s explanations. Some questions by design require multi-turn interactions to arrive at the correct answer, in order to assess conversational coherence and context handling. We randomize the order of agents, and although the question types remain consistent across conditions, specific values (e.g., instance identifiers) are varied to mitigate learning effects.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个智能体，参与者完成三个任务。 这些任务涵盖既有XAI问题分类体系（Liao等人，2020）中的多个类别， 包括数据理解、局部解释和反事实检验。 每个任务至少包含两个问题，所有任务共九个问题。 这些问题从每个任务预先定义好的多选题库中抽取（详见附录D.1节）。 这些问题的设计使得可以借助智能体解释所提供的基本真实信息来作答。 有些问题在设计上需要多轮交互才能得出正确答案，以便评估对话连贯性和上下文处理能力。 我们对智能体的顺序进行了随机化，尽管各条件下的问题类型保持一致，但具体取值（例如实例标识符）会加以变化，以减轻学习效应。

paragraphs.en: We collect both, objective and subjective measures. Objective metrics are (1) answer accuracy, (2) conversational efficiency measured as the number of turns per correctly answered question, which is commonly used in dialogue agent evaluation Su et al. (2016) ; Peng et al. (2017) , and (3) indicators of conversational breakdowns, such as repeated or rephrased questions and agent failures, where the agent does not provide meaningful answers. Subjective measures consist of two parts. First, we use the 5-point Likert BUS-11 usability scale Borsci and Schmettow (2024) , which includes 11 items across five subscales, focusing on perceived conversation and information quality and perceived chatbot functionality. Second, we include a pairwise comparison questionnaire between the two agents to assess user preference and explanation effectiveness.
paragraphs.zh: 我们同时收集客观和主观两类测量指标。 客观指标包括：(1) 答案准确性；(2) 对话效率，即每个被正确回答的问题所需的对话轮数，这一指标在对话智能体评估中被广泛使用 Su et al. (2016)；Peng et al. (2017)；以及 (3) 对话中断的指标，例如重复提问或换一种方式提问，以及智能体未能提供有意义回答的失败情况。 主观测量由两部分组成。 首先，我们采用 5 点李克特量表的 BUS-11 可用性量表 Borsci and Schmettow (2024)，该量表包含五个子量表共 11 个条目，侧重于对对话质量与信息质量的感知，以及对聊天机器人功能的感知。 其次，我们加入两个智能体之间的两两比较问卷，以评估用户偏好和解释的有效性。

paragraphs.en: Replacing TalkToModel ’s conversational component with SimXAI leads to clear improvements in both, task performance and perceived interaction quality. Table 5 shows that participants achieve substantially higher accuracy with SimXAI than with the original TalkToModel (92.1% vs. 59.0%, p < .001 p<.001 ). SimXAI also reduces interaction costs: users complete the task in fewer turns on average (10.0 vs. 12.4 turns) and in less time (5.8 vs. 7.4 minutes). Across all sessions, this translates to roughly half as many turns per correct answer with SimXAI (1.32 vs. 2.70).

paragraphs.en: Besides the systems analyzed in § 2 , that rely on fine-tuned models, off-the-shelf LLMs are increasingly adopted in ConvXAI. Nguyen et al. (2024) extend XAgent by Llama-2 Touvron et al. (2023) for postprocessing NLG and answering general factual questions (e.g., about machine learning terminology). KnowThySelf Prasai et al. (2025) is a multi-agent framework, which at its core still resembles the GUS architecture. It employs Gemma3-27B Team et al. (2025) for most parts of NLU and NLG, while user intents are matched to specialized agents by embedding-based similarity, using nomic-embed-text Nussbaum et al. (2025) . These specialized agents encapsulate XAI resources. Closest to our work is Echo Vanbrabant et al. (2025) , another agentic framework with a tool-calling LLM at its core. However, Echo trades faithfulness for human validation “… might not always result in a helpful or correct answer […] This further highlights the importance of human-in-the-loop workflows, in which the LLM can try again until the answer is satisfactory”. This undermines the purpose of ConvXAI to explain a model’s true reasoning, as any plausible answer is likely satisfactory. Yet, plausibility and correctness are different evaluation criteria that should not be conflated Nauta et al. (2023) (a plausible answer might not be correct, while a correct one might not be plausible, e.g., if the model’s reasoning is flawed).

paragraphs.en: All these systems are demos without quantitative or qualitative evaluation. Unlike prior GUS-based systems or existing tool-calling ConvXAI agents, our contribution is not the generic tool-calling mechanism itself. SimXAI introduces a simple, lightweight, open-source intermediate layer with a ConvXAI-specific separation between conversational control and underlying XAI resources, an extensible XAI function design, and a dedicated evaluation suite. The measured faithfulness in this suite is response-to-tool faithfulness and should not be interpreted as validation of the backend explanation method.

paragraphs.en: SimXAI enables natural conversational interactions with existing XAI resources through general callable functions. Across evaluations of parsing, response-to-tool faithfulness, and contextualization, its lightweight LLM-centric design supports conversational explanations while usually preserving the information returned by the XAI resources. Our user study shows that replacing the conversational layers of a traditional GUS-based ConvXAI agent by SimXAI significantly improves task performance and perceived interaction quality. This suggests that LLM-centric architectures provide tangible benefits to users in understanding AI model behavior. In future work, we plan to explore and enhance fully automated evaluation for LLM-based conversational XAI layers. Based on that, we plan to study how LLM choice affects tool calling and to develop further improvements to ConvXAI.
paragraphs.zh: SimXAI 通过通用可调用函数，实现与现有 XAI 资源的自然对话式交互。 在解析、响应与工具的一致性以及情境化等方面的评估中，其以大语言模型为中心的轻量级设计能够在通常保留 XAI 资源所返回信息的同时，支持对话式解释。 我们的用户研究表明，用 SimXAI 替换基于传统 GUS 的 ConvXAI 智能体的对话层，可显著提升任务表现和用户感知的交互质量。 这表明以大语言模型为中心的架构能为用户理解 AI 模型行为带来切实的收益。 在未来工作中，我们计划探索并增强针对基于大语言模型的对话式 XAI 层的全自动化评估。 在此基础上，我们计划研究大语言模型的选择如何影响工具调用，并进一步改进 ConvXAI。

paragraphs.en: Table 3 To build the multi-turn version (Figure 6 , right side), related consecutive questions that operated on the same input text were grouped together into multi-turn conversation sets. Specifically, questions that originally repeated the full instance text had those explicit instance references replaced with pronouns like “it” turning them into natural follow-up turns. This way, the conversation flows naturally: the first turn establishes the target text, and subsequent turns refer back to it implicitly — just as a human would in real dialogue. In total, we created 10 multi-turn dialogues with averaging 4–6 turns each.

paragraphs.en: Specifically, we asked five members of our research group with a background in machine learning to assess the realism of user utterances in the synthetically generated explanatory conversations. Participants were asked to imagine themselves as users seeking to understand how a classification model makes its decisions. They were then presented with generated dialogues between a User and an Explainer . paragraphs.en: As shown in Table 10 , SimXAI substantially improves users’ ability to answer explanation-related questions correctly. If we count all cases when users indicated that the question is not answerable (“unable to answer”) as incorrect, accuracy increases from 53.3 ± \pm 19.6 with TalkToModel to 84.1 ± \pm 17.7 with SimXAI . The same pattern holds when excluding unable to answer responses from the denominator, with accuracy increasing from 59.0 ± \pm 21.3 to 92.1 ± \pm 11.6. The corresponding paired tests in Table 12 confirm that both improvements are highly significant ( p < .001 p<.001 in both cases).
paragraphs.zh: 如表 10 所示，SimXAI 显著提升了用户正确回答与解释相关问题的能力。 如果将用户表示问题无法回答（“无法回答”）的所有情况均计为错误，准确率从使用 TalkToModel 时的 53.3 ± \pm 19.6 提升至使用 SimXAI 时的 84.1 ± \pm 17.7。 在从分母中排除“无法回答”的回复时，也呈现出同样的模式，准确率从 59.0 ± \pm 21.3 提升至 92.1 ± \pm 11.6。 表 12 中相应的配对检验证实，这两项提升均具有高度显著性（两种情况下均为 p < .001 p<.001）。

paragraphs.en: SimXAI also made interactions more efficient. paragraphs.en: Overall, the results across Tables 10 – 9 show a consistent pattern: replacing TalkToModel ’s conversational component with SimXAI improves answer quality, increases task success, reduces interaction cost, and leads to more favorable user judgments. The clearest gains appear on aspects that matter most for explanation-oriented multi-turn interaction, namely clarity, contextual coherence, helpfulness, and efficiency.
